# Draft:Sh. M. Anwaruzzaman

=
Sh. M. Anwaruzzaman (1 February 1935 – 8 April 2026) was a Bangladeshi educator and freedom fighter known for his long-term contribution to secondary and higher education in Lohagara, Narail District. He played a significant role in the development of educational institutions in the region and was recognized by the Government of Bangladesh as a freedom fighter.
Early life
Anwaruzzaman was born on 1 February 1935 in Lohagara, Narail District, then part of British India. He grew up in the region during a period of educational and political transition in Bengal.
Career
Teaching and administrative roles
Anwaruzzaman began his professional career in education as a teacher and later served as the headmaster of [http://www.lphs.edu.bd/ Lohagara Government Pilot High School]. Through his academic leadership, he contributed to the development of local secondary education infrastructure.
He later served as the principal of Lohagara Government Adarsha College. During his tenure, he was involved in strengthening institutional administration and academic structure.
Contribution to Lohagara Government Adarsha College
Anwaruzzaman was associated with the early development of Lohagara Government Adarsha College, which was established in 1968. According to national press reporting, he was among the educators involved in the institutional development process during its early years.
The college was initially established through local educational initiatives and later expanded into a government institution in 2013. His involvement is noted in accounts of the institution’s early development period.
Bangladesh Liberation War
During the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971, Anwaruzzaman was associated with local-level organizing activities supporting the independence movement. He is officially listed as a recognized freedom fighter by the Government of Bangladesh.
His name appears in official records maintained by the government regarding freedom fighter recognition.
Later life and death
Anwaruzzaman died on 8 April 2026 in Dhaka. He was buried in Lohagara with state recognition. His death was reported in local media outlets, and tributes were published highlighting his contributions to education and public service.

Legacy
Anwaruzzaman is remembered in Lohagara for his role in education development and institutional leadership. Following his death, local institutions and community organizations acknowledged his contributions to the growth of education in the region.
